description: Comprehensive question bank based on 'Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence' (KEA FDA & SDA Examination). Questions are structured to cover all topics, sub-topics, and high-yield facts from the provided PDF notes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What does social change refer to in the context of Karnataka after Independence?

options.A: Only changes in the political system
options.B: Significant changes in the structure, institutions, values, relationships, and opportunities of society over time
options.C: Changes only in the economic sector
options.D: Changes in the geographical boundaries of the state

questions.explanation: Social change refers to significant changes in the structure, institutions, values, relationships, and opportunities of society over time, influenced by constitutional democracy, education, economic development, land reforms, industrialisation, urbanisation, and social movements.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a major force contributing to social change in Karnataka after 1947?

options.B: Land reforms

questions.explanation: The major forces included the Constitution and laws, land reforms, expansion of education, public employment, reservation, democratic politics, migration, industrial growth, urbanisation, women's movements, backward-class movements, Dalit movements, and tribal welfare programmes. Colonial rule was before 1947.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Why is the year 1956 important in the political and social history of Karnataka?

options.A: Karnataka was renamed from Mysore State
options.B: The States Reorganisation Act was passed, reorganising states on linguistic lines
options.C: The Constitution of India came into effect
options.D: The first Panchayati Raj elections were held

questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised states on linguistic lines and brought Kannada-speaking regions together in the enlarged Mysore State, creating a common administrative framework.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: When was Mysore State officially renamed Karnataka?

options.B: 1 November 1973

questions.explanation: Mysore State was officially renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Did social change after Independence remove all traditional inequalities in Karnataka?

options.B: No, caste discrimination, gender inequality, economic disparities, landlessness, and regional imbalances continued

questions.explanation: Social change expanded rights, opportunities, and political participation, but caste discrimination, gender inequality, economic disparities, landlessness, and regional imbalances continued.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?

options.B: Article 15

questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which law gives effect to the constitutional abolition of untouchability?

options.A: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.B: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, originally enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, penalises the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which law specifically addresses atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.B: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides for prevention of specified offences, special courts, and relief and rehabilitation measures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is meant by the decline of traditional jajmani relations?

options.A: The strengthening of hereditary caste-linked exchanges
options.B: The weakening of hereditary, caste-linked exchanges of services and payments between dominant landholding families and service or artisan castes

questions.explanation: It refers to the weakening of hereditary, caste-linked exchanges of services and payments between dominant landholding families and service or artisan castes, partly due to markets, wage labour, migration, and new occupations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Did caste disappear from Karnataka's urban society?

options.B: No, it continued to influence marriage networks, associations, housing access, social networks, and political mobilisation
options.D: No, but only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Urbanisation and modern occupations reduced some forms of everyday caste dependence, but caste continued to influence marriage networks, associations, housing access, social networks, and political mobilisation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is caste-based political mobilisation?

options.A: The organisation of people around caste identity to seek representation, public resources, recognition, and policy benefits through democratic institutions
options.B: The abolition of caste

questions.explanation: Caste-based political mobilisation is the organisation of people around caste identity or shared caste-related interests to seek representation, public resources, recognition, and policy benefits through democratic institutions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which sociologist developed the concept of the dominant caste?

options.B: M. N. Srinivas

questions.explanation: Mysore-born sociologist M. N. Srinivas developed the concept of the dominant caste in Indian sociology.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is a dominant caste in sociological analysis?

options.A: A caste that is numerically the smallest
options.B: A locally influential caste whose strength may derive from landownership, numerical presence, economic resources, education, and political influence
options.C: A caste that has no political influence
options.D: A caste that is only involved in agriculture

questions.explanation: A dominant caste is a locally influential caste whose strength may derive from landownership, numerical presence, economic resources, education, and political influence; the term is associated with sociologist M. N. Srinivas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which two communities have historically been identified as major dominant agrarian communities in parts of Karnataka?

options.B: Lingayats and Vokkaligas

questions.explanation: Lingayats and Vokkaligas have historically held substantial agrarian, economic, and political influence in different regions, although Karnataka's social structure is diverse and locally variable.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?

options.B: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and came into force on 24 April 1993.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What are the three commonly recognised tiers of rural local government in Karnataka?

options.A: Gram Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, Zilla Panchayat
options.B: Ward Committee, Municipality, Corporation
options.C: Gram Sabha, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad
options.D: Village Council, Block Council, District Council

questions.explanation: The three tiers are Gram Panchayat at village level, Taluk Panchayat at taluk level, and Zilla Panchayat at district level.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the effect of rural-to-urban migration on village society?

options.B: It changes labour availability, household income, and aspirations; remittances may support education, housing, and consumption, while migration can also create labour shortages and family separation
options.C: It leads to the complete collapse of village society
options.D: It has no effect on village society

questions.explanation: Migration changes labour availability, household income, and aspirations; remittances may support education, housing, and consumption, while migration can also create labour shortages and family separation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is meant by rural social stratification?

options.A: The equal distribution of land and resources
options.B: The unequal distribution of land, income, occupation, status, and power among groups in rural society, often shaped by caste, class, gender, and access to public resources
options.C: The migration of people from rural to urban areas

questions.explanation: It is the unequal distribution of land, income, occupation, status, and power among groups in rural society, often shaped by caste, class, gender, and access to public resources.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a fundamental right?

options.B: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 a fundamental right.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the Right to Education Act?

options.A: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
options.B: The Right to Information Act, 2005
options.C: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 gives children aged 6 to 14 a legal entitlement to free and compulsory elementary education under Article 21A.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is a continuing challenge in educational development in Karnataka?

options.B: Differences in school quality, learning outcomes, digital access, language resources, household income, gender, and rural-urban infrastructure
options.D: Overcrowding in schools only in urban areas

questions.explanation: Differences in school quality, learning outcomes, digital access, language resources, household income, gender, and rural-urban infrastructure continue to affect educational equality.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which city is widely known as the Silicon Valley of India?

options.B: Mangaluru

questions.explanation: Bengaluru is widely known as the Silicon Valley of India because of its concentration of information technology, software, start-up, and related industries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an important industrial centre in Karnataka apart from Bengaluru?

options.B: Mangaluru

questions.explanation: Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Ballari, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, and the Kolar region are among the state's important industrial or commercial centres. Chennai is in Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What problems can accompany rapid urbanisation?

options.B: Housing shortages, slums and informal settlements, traffic congestion, air and water pollution, pressure on water supply, waste management problems, unequal services, and loss of open spaces

questions.explanation: Common problems include housing shortages, slums and informal settlements, traffic congestion, air and water pollution, pressure on water supply, waste management problems, unequal services, and loss of open spaces.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: How did industrialisation change the occupational structure in Karnataka?

options.B: It expanded employment in factories, transport, construction, engineering, services, and formal or informal wage work, reducing exclusive dependence on agriculture
options.D: It had no effect on occupational structure

questions.explanation: It expanded employment in factories, transport, construction, engineering, services, and formal or informal wage work, reducing the exclusive dependence of many households on agriculture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution permits special provisions for women and children?

options.B: Article 15(3)

questions.explanation: Article 15(3) permits special provisions for women and children.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Directive Principle directs the State to ensure equal pay for men and women?

options.B: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 39(d) directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?

options.B: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 42 directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment provides reservation for women in Panchayats?

options.B: 74th Constitutional Amendment

questions.explanation: Article 243D, introduced through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, requires reservation of not less than one-third of seats for women in Panchayats.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment provides reservation for women in Municipalities?

options.B: 74th Constitutional Amendment

questions.explanation: Article 243T, introduced through the 74th Constitutional Amendment, provides reservation of not less than one-third of seats for women in Municipalities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the significance of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 for women?

options.A: It provides the state-law framework for Panchayat institutions and reservation in local governance, helping widen women's participation
options.B: It abolished Panchayati Raj
options.C: It only applies to urban local bodies

questions.explanation: It provides the state-law framework for Panchayat institutions and reservation in local governance, helping widen women's participation in grassroots democracy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What are Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and how can they empower women?

options.A: Large government organisations that provide direct employment
options.B: Small voluntary groups, often formed by women, that promote regular savings, access to credit, collective enterprise, mutual support, and participation in local development

questions.explanation: SHGs are small voluntary groups, often formed by women, that promote regular savings, access to credit, collective enterprise, mutual support, and participation in local development.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is a major continuing barrier to women's empowerment?

options.B: Gender-based violence, unequal unpaid care work, wage gaps, limited asset ownership, restrictions on mobility, and under-representation in some decision-making spaces

questions.explanation: Gender-based violence, unequal unpaid care work, wage gaps, limited asset ownership, restrictions on mobility, and under-representation in some decision-making spaces remain important barriers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is social mobility?

options.A: The movement of individuals or groups from one social or economic position to another within a society
options.B: The migration of people from one country to another
options.C: The physical movement of people from rural to urban areas

questions.explanation: Social mobility is the movement of individuals or groups from one social or economic position to another within a society.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is upward social mobility?

options.A: Movement to a lower socio-economic position
options.B: Movement to a higher socio-economic position through education, occupation, income, political influence, or other changes
options.C: Movement from urban to rural areas
options.D: Movement from one caste to another

questions.explanation: Upward social mobility occurs when a person or group moves to a higher socio-economic position through education, occupation, income, political influence, or other changes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is intergenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in social or economic position during an individual's own lifetime
options.B: A change in social or economic position between parents and their children
options.C: Movement from one country to another
options.D: Movement from one caste to another

questions.explanation: Intergenerational mobility refers to a change in social or economic position between parents and their children.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is intragenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in social or economic position during an individual's own lifetime
options.B: A change in social or economic position between parents and their children
options.C: Movement from one country to another
options.D: Movement from one caste to another

questions.explanation: Intragenerational mobility refers to a change in an individual's social or economic position during that person's own lifetime.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is Sanskritisation?

options.A: A process where a lower-ranking caste or community seeks upward status by adopting practices and rituals associated with groups regarded as higher in the local caste hierarchy
options.B: The adoption of Western culture

questions.explanation: Sanskritisation is a process described by M. N. Srinivas in which a lower-ranking caste or community seeks upward status by adopting practices and rituals associated with groups regarded as higher in the local caste hierarchy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is Westernisation in Indian sociology?

options.A: A process where lower castes adopt higher caste practices
options.B: A concept used by M. N. Srinivas referring to changes in Indian society associated with contact with Western institutions, technology, education, values, and ways of life

questions.explanation: Westernisation, a concept used by M. N. Srinivas, refers to changes in Indian society associated with contact with Western institutions, technology, education, values, and ways of life.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the difference between Sanskritisation and Westernisation?

options.A: Sanskritisation involves adopting Western practices, while Westernisation involves adopting higher caste practices
options.B: Sanskritisation involves adopting practices associated with higher-status groups within the caste order, whereas Westernisation refers to changes associated with Western influence in institutions, technology, education, and culture
options.D: Sanskritisation is only about language, while Westernisation is only about technology

questions.explanation: Sanskritisation involves adopting practices associated with higher-status groups within the caste order, whereas Westernisation refers to changes associated with Western influence in institutions, technology, education, and culture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Does social mobility mean that caste inequalities have ended?

options.B: No, individuals and groups may experience mobility while caste continues to shape marriage, social networks, discrimination, access to resources, and political representation
options.C: Yes, but only in urban areas
options.D: No, because social mobility is impossible

questions.explanation: No. Individuals and groups may experience mobility while caste continues to shape marriage, social networks, discrimination, access to resources, and political representation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?

options.B: Article 330

questions.explanation: Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is reservation in the Indian constitutional context?

options.A: A form of affirmative action that provides specified representation or opportunities to constitutionally recognised or legally identified disadvantaged groups
options.B: The process of booking train tickets
options.C: The reservation of seats in private clubs

questions.explanation: Reservation is a form of affirmative action that provides specified representation or opportunities to constitutionally recognised or legally identified disadvantaged groups in areas such as education, public employment, and elected bodies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article enables special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and SCs and STs in education?

options.B: Article 16(4)

questions.explanation: Article 15(4), inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951, enables special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and for SCs and STs.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article permits reservation in public employment for backward classes inadequately represented in State services?

options.B: Article 16(4)

questions.explanation: Article 16(4) permits the State to make provision for reservation of appointments or posts in favour of a backward class of citizens that, in the State's opinion, is not adequately represented in its services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?

options.B: Article 330

questions.explanation: Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies?

options.B: Article 330

questions.explanation: Article 332 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What does Article 16(4A) enable?

options.A: Reservation in matters of promotion for SCs and STs under the conditions stated in the Constitution and interpreted by the courts
options.B: Reservation in education for backward classes

questions.explanation: Article 16(4A) enables reservation in matters of promotion for SCs and STs under the conditions stated in the Constitution and interpreted by the courts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the difference between political reservation and reservation in public employment?

options.A: Political reservation reserves seats in elected legislative or local bodies; employment reservation concerns appointments or posts in public services
options.B: Political reservation is for SCs/STs only; employment reservation is for women only
options.D: Political reservation is for backward classes; employment reservation is for SCs/STs

questions.explanation: Political reservation reserves seats in elected legislative or local bodies; employment reservation concerns appointments or posts in public services under relevant constitutional provisions and laws.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the significance of the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments for representation?

options.A: They constitutionalised rural and urban local self-government and provided reservation for SCs, STs, and women in local bodies
options.B: They abolished local self-government
options.C: They only provided reservation in Parliament
options.D: They only apply to urban areas

questions.explanation: They constitutionalised rural and urban local self-government and provided reservation for SCs, STs, and women in local bodies, with details governed by the Constitution and state legislation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Who was D. Devaraj Urs and why is he important in Karnataka's social history?

options.A: He was the first Chief Minister of Karnataka
options.B: He was Chief Minister of Karnataka during much of the 1970s and is associated with policies aimed at broadening political representation and advancing backward classes
options.C: He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee
options.D: He was a famous Kannada poet

questions.explanation: D. Devaraj Urs was Chief Minister of Karnataka during much of the 1970s and is associated with policies aimed at broadening political representation and advancing backward classes and other disadvantaged groups.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: In which year did the Karnataka Backward Classes Welfare Department originate as a separate welfare administration under Devaraj Urs?
questions.explanation: The Mysuru district government's official account states that Devaraj Urs established the Backward Classes Welfare Department in 1977.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which constitutional provisions are cited by Karnataka's Backward Classes Welfare Department for its mandate?

options.B: Articles 15(4) and 16(4)

questions.explanation: Articles 15(4) and 16(4) are cited as constitutional bases for special provisions in education and reservation in public employment for eligible backward classes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What was the Havanur Commission?

options.A: Karnataka's First Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1975 under L. G. Havanur
options.B: Karnataka's Second Backward Classes Commission

questions.explanation: The Havanur Commission was Karnataka's First Backward Classes Commission, appointed by the Devaraj Urs government in 1975 under L. G. Havanur to study social and educational backwardness and recommend measures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What was the Venkataswamy Commission?

options.B: Karnataka's Second Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1983

questions.explanation: The Venkataswamy Commission, appointed in 1983, was Karnataka's Second Backward Classes Commission and undertook a statewide socio-economic and educational survey before submitting recommendations in 1986.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What was the Chinnappa Reddy Commission?

options.B: Karnataka's Second Backward Classes Commission
options.C: Karnataka's Third Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1990

questions.explanation: The Chinnappa Reddy Commission was Karnataka's Third Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1990 and associated with recommendations on backward-class identification and reservation policy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What was the significance of the 1970s backward-class mobilisation in Karnataka?

options.A: It widened political debate about representation and social justice beyond established dominant political groups and helped bring backward-class welfare to the centre of state policy
options.B: It led to the abolition of reservation
options.D: It had no impact on state policy

questions.explanation: It widened political debate about representation and social justice beyond established dominant political groups and helped bring backward-class welfare and inclusion to the centre of state policy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which national leader and thinker strongly influenced modern Dalit movements in India?

options.B: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar strongly influenced modern Dalit movements through his struggle against untouchability and caste discrimination and his advocacy of education, organisation, agitation, and constitutional rights.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the Bhusa/Bhoosa controversy associated with B. Basavalingappa in Karnataka?

options.B: A controversy that arose in 1973 when Karnataka minister B. Basavalingappa criticised the dominance of what he called 'boosa' in Kannada literature, provoking a major public debate on caste representation, cultural exclusion, and Dalit assertion

questions.explanation: The controversy arose in 1973 when Karnataka minister B. Basavalingappa criticised the dominance of what he called 'boosa' in Kannada literature, provoking a major public debate on caste representation, cultural exclusion, and Dalit assertion.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is the Dalita Sangharsha Samiti (DSS)?

options.B: A Dalit rights organisation and movement in Karnataka that mobilised against untouchability, caste oppression, exploitation, and denial of rights

questions.explanation: The Dalita Sangharsha Samiti is a Dalit rights organisation and movement in Karnataka that mobilised against untouchability, caste oppression, exploitation, and denial of rights.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: During which period did the Dalita Sangharsha Samiti emerge as a major force in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The DSS emerged as a major organised force in the 1970s, with its growth linked to the wider Dalit assertion of that period.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What were the major issues raised by the Karnataka Dalit movement?

options.B: Untouchability, atrocities, land rights, access to common resources, dignity, education, labour exploitation, gender oppression, representation, and the annihilation of caste

questions.explanation: Its concerns included untouchability, atrocities, land rights, access to common resources, dignity, education, labour exploitation, gender oppression, representation, and the annihilation of caste.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: What is Dalit literature?

options.B: Writing that expresses and examines the lived experiences, oppression, resistance, identity, and aspirations of Dalit communities, often challenging caste-based social structures
options.C: Literature written by upper castes about Dalits

questions.explanation: Dalit literature is writing that expresses and examines the lived experiences, oppression, resistance, identity, and aspirations of Dalit communities, often challenging caste-based social structures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Article empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes?

options.B: Article 342

questions.explanation: Article 342 empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory, subject to the constitutional procedure for subsequent changes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Article provides for administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in most states?

options.B: Sixth Schedule

questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule provides for administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than the areas covered by the Sixth Schedule.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Article provides for a National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.B: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 338A provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which Constitutional Article directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections?

options.B: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Social Changes
questions.chapter: Social Changes in Karnataka After Independence
questions.question: Which of the following is a Scheduled Tribe community found in Karnataka?
